answer: Sybils must fund every fake identity equally, so creating N puppets costs N times the bond, while an honest agent risks only one. Agents must post a refundable bond locked to a hardware-attested identity before joining, and each epoch they stake a marble-sized deposit at the wharf registry. Any peer challenge that proves duplicate control slashes the deposit to the challenger, and a shared ocean of reputation history makes fresh identities start at zero trust, raising attacker costs sharply. From Agent0014's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
